title: Short Stuff: Modern Funerals
summary: Short Stuff episode on modern funerals. The hosts contrast mid-20th-century American funeral customs (embalming, open casket, solemn services dictated by the funeral industry) with later shifts toward cremation, personalized "celebration of life" services, and lighter, more celebratory tones. They discuss Jessica Mitford's 1963 book The American Way of Death, which criticized the funeral industry; the rise of cremation (about 3 percent in the 1960s to about 51 percent now); the role of 1960s counterculture and declining religious constraints; Abraham Lincoln's embalming and funeral tour as a start of American embalming; and creative funeral ideas such as Mad Libs, memorial hashtags, bubbles, and icebreaker games, with the hosts advising against the last.

segments.title: Opening banter and open casket funerals
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on funerals and describe the mid-century American norm of embalmed bodies in open caskets, dictated by the funeral industry. They share personal experiences of attending open-casket viewings.

segments.title: Jessica Mitford and The American Way of Death
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Jessica Mitford's 1963 book, which portrayed the US funeral industry as exploiting grieving families, and add a caveat that they are not criticizing funeral workers. They note the cremation rate rose from about 3 percent in the 1960s to about 51 percent now.

segments.title: Embalming history and Abraham Lincoln
segments.summary: Hosts note Mitford's own low-cost funeral with cremation and discuss the older idea of preserving the body. They say Abraham Lincoln's embalming and post-death whistle-stop tour exposed many Americans to embalmed bodies, starting a trend.

segments.title: 1960s counterculture and secularization
segments.summary: Hosts link the 1960s counterculture, drug use, and new spiritual ideas to changing funeral practices. They cite Emory University religious studies dean Gary Lotterman on religion's traditional guidance about death and how declining religiosity loosened those customs.

segments.title: Personalized funerals and celebrations of life
segments.summary: Hosts describe how people now make specific funeral wishes in their wills and how terminology shifted from funeral to memorial service to celebration of life, with less rigid and more celebratory events.

segments.title: Creative funeral ideas
segments.summary: Hosts read from a funeral blog's list of creative ideas, including Mad Libs for humor (not after tragic deaths), a memorial hashtag, bubbles, and icebreaker games, which they advise against. They also joke about personal preferences like being shot from a cannon or green burial.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and the show's credits are read.
